correctness.rationale: For any chosen nonblock four-set A, each of its four 3-subsets has a different completion outside A: otherwise two distinct blocks would share a triple, contradicting the Steiner axiom. There are exactly v-8 unused fifth-move generic points. For a block four-set all unused points generic; after a three-set there is one triple-completion and other generic points. These atomic extension spectra coincide across all SQS through four moves, and at five moves across v>=10. A five-quantifier sentence selecting a nonblock 4-set plus a fifth point outside all four completion types separates order 8 from order >=10; Hanani orders 8 and 10 exist. No greater-rank or block-sorted language theorem is claimed. Independently constructed Boolean SQS(8), SQS(16), verified each triple once and all nonblock extension counts (0 and 8).
